headline: Highest risk is medium: Superset can egress to allowlisted APIs while Marker has no filesystem/network surfaces, so interaction risks are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. Marker has no filesystem, browser, subprocess, or MCP surfaces, and Superset only exposes a Superset API with allowlisted egress. Without a bridge, there is no plausible default prompt-injection pathway between them.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies Marker output into Superset prompts or API payloads, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Require explicit human review before any Marker output is pasted into Superset.
Disable any automation that forwards document text into Superset prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on any cross-agent content transfer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Marker is local-only by profile, while Superset has allowlisted network egress and API access. There is no documented shared workspace or sensitive data class, so leakage is not established; however, if Marker output is forwarded into Superset, Superset could transmit it outward.
conditions: IF Marker output contains sensitive document text and is passed into Superset, that text may leave the local boundary.
IF Superset is configured to query remote services with imported content, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not route confidential documents from Marker into Superset.
Restrict Superset to non-sensitive datasets only.
Review outbound API destinations in Superset before use.
requires-engineering: enforce content classification gates on cross-agent transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, and Superset exposes no write-capable filesystem or git surface in the profile. With no overlapping mutable resource, a capability conflict pathway is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk appears.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, the assessment changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only with respect to shared artifacts.
Avoid mounting the same writable directory into both agents.
Separate any git workflows from these agents.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marker produces document-processing output that Superset could ingest through its API, so A-to-B chaining is plausible. The profiles do not show verification or critique steps in Superset, so if Marker output is treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream analytics or actions.
conditions: IF Superset ingests Marker output without validation, erroneous extracted facts can propagate.
IF downstream dashboards or reports are generated from that ingested output, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Add a manual verification step before Superset ingestion.
Sample-check Marker extractions against source documents.
Limit Superset to staging datasets until accuracy is confirmed.
requires-engineering: implement schema and confidence checks on imported fields.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either agent. The profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or mismatched compliance obligations, so a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent, compliance review is required.
IF residency or retention policies differ for future deployments, reassess.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair until policies are defined.
Document retention and residency settings before deployment.
Review access controls for any future sensitive datasets.
